headline: Canada desk: Christina Lake rejects bids; Decibel moves to OTCQX
dek: Christina Lake Cannabis turned down two takeover approaches, Decibel upgraded its US listing on 13 November, and Health Canada revoked Sirona Pharma's licence.
key_points: Christina Lake Cannabis said on 10 November it will stay independent after a board committee rejected an offer for its shares and a separate bid for its assets.
StratCann reported the two approaches were worth about C$15 million and C$18 million; the company said neither offered enough value.
Decibel Cannabis began trading on the OTCQX Best Market on 13 November, upgrading from OTCQB to court more US investors.
Health Canada listed Sirona Pharma's licence as revoked on request on 13 November, as the company winds up after creditor protection.
body: Three smaller Canadian producers made news this week, each showing a different way companies in the country's crowded market are trying to get through it. Christina Lake Cannabis, a large outdoor grower in British Columbia, said it will stay independent after rejecting two takeover approaches. Decibel Cannabis moved its US share listing up a tier to reach American investors. And Sirona Pharma, which has been winding down under creditor protection, gave up its Health Canada licence.
None of these is a large deal by itself. Together they show buyers circling cheap assets, sellers holding out for better prices, and the steady exit of companies that could not make the numbers work.
## Christina Lake says no to both bids

Christina Lake Cannabis announced on 10 November that a special committee of its board had finished reviewing two unsolicited proposals and recommended against both. The first, announced on 21 August, was a non-binding letter of intent from a private Alberta company to buy all of the company's shares. The second, announced on 15 September, was an offer from a separate party to buy substantially all of its assets. StratCann reported the share offer was worth C$15 million and the asset offer, from Ontario's Medical Saints, C$18 million.

The committee made its recommendation on 26 October and the board accepted it, the company said. It concluded that neither proposal offered enough value to recommend to shareholders or to win their approval. It pointed to a strong 2026 harvest, a sharper focus on growing and selling flower, efforts to cut costs and expand cultivation, and continued debt repayment. No definitive agreement was signed with either party.

Christina Lake runs a 32-acre licensed site with more than 950,000 square feet of outdoor growing space and a separate 342-acre property with about 100 acres licensed for outdoor growing, according to MMJ Daily. Its shares trade on the Canadian Securities Exchange as CLC.
> When a grower turns down an offer for all of its assets, it is betting the harvest is worth more than the land and licences under it.
## Decibel steps up its US listing

Decibel Cannabis, based in Calgary, began trading on the OTCQX Best Market on 13 November under its existing symbol DBCCF, after qualifying to move up from the OTCQB Venture Market. OTC Markets Group says companies on OTCQX must meet higher financial standards and follow best-practice governance. Decibel's shares continue to trade on the TSX Venture Exchange as DB.

The company, known for the General Admission, Qwest and Standard Issue brands, runs a processing plant in Calgary, a cultivation site in Battleford, Saskatchewan, and an EU-GMP licensed cultivation and processing facility in Chatham, Ontario, which serves its export business. Chief executive Benjamin Sze said the move is a way to reach more US investors.

For a Canadian producer listed on the TSX Venture Exchange, an OTCQX upgrade is a modest step: it does not bring a US exchange listing, but it puts the shares on the over-the-counter tier with the strictest disclosure and governance standards, which some US investors require before buying.

Health Canada listed Sirona Pharma's licence as revoked on request on 13 November, StratCann reported in its weekly round-up. The company had been winding up its creditor protection process. A licence surrendered on request ends its ability to cultivate or process cannabis legally.

Other figures from the week show where money is moving. British Columbia has collected C$617.9 million from its share of federal cannabis excise taxes through June 2026, including C$70.4 million in the first half of this year, StratCann reported. Brazil's medical cannabis market brought in C$122.2 million in sales in the 12 months to August 2026, up 15%, according to StratCann. On the large-deal side, as we reported on 12 November, Curaleaf has cleared German and Canadian competition reviews for its bid for Aurora Cannabis, while Organigram's rival offer still needs shareholder, court and regulatory approval.

Watch whether either suitor comes back to Christina Lake with a higher offer, and whether the company's harvest shows up in its next quarterly results. For Decibel, the test is whether the OTCQX listing lifts US trading volume. More broadly, the Aurora contest between Curaleaf and Organigram will set the tone for valuations of Canadian producers, large and small, into 2027.
